mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing of each corporate UBO (shareholder)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign company registry in the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (Egypt is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention; document must be legalized by the Egyptian consulate in the issuing jurisdiction)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copy of each ultimate individual beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Passport Authority of the individual's citizenship
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (Egyptian consulate certification + Arabic certified translation)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming the opening of a provisional corporate account or pre-incorporation account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed Egyptian bank (e.g., National Bank of Egypt, Banque Misr, Commercial International Bank)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Internal banking notarization; no external legalization required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Memorandum of Association (MOA) and Articles of Association (AOA) in Arabic
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Draft prepared by Egyptian licensed corporate lawyer; notarized by an Egyptian Notary Public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Egyptian Notary Public certification and registration with the Commercial Registry

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against the Egyptian Financial Intelligence Unit (EMLCU) lists, the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and domestic high-risk country lists. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) is statutorily required for all politically exposed persons (PEPs, including foreign and domestic PEPs, their family members, and close associates) under Law No. 80/2002 and CBE regulations. Continuous transaction monitoring and risk-based customer due diligence at 25% ownership threshold.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Egypt Commercial Registry Portal (via GAFI One-Stop Shop, https://www.gafi.gov.eg)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official company name must be in Arabic; an English transliteration is permitted as a secondary name. The LLC name must contain the suffix 'الشركة ذات مسؤولية محدودة' ('LLC' or 'Sharikat Dhat Mas'uliyah Mahdudah') unless abbreviated in a legally approved form. The transliteration must follow the Amended Arabic Romanization Table standards accepted by GAFI; a matching English trade name may be registered.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant may submit a written administrative appeal to the GAFI Name Clearance Committee within 15 working days of the rejection notification. The appeal must include the refused name, a certified copy of the reservation request, and grounds for reconsideration. The Committee must issue a written decision within 30 days. If the appeal decision is still adverse, the applicant may commence judicial review before the Administrative Court of the State Council (Cairo) within 60 days of the final administrative rejection.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permitted for NVOCC licensing. A physical office address in Egypt is unconditionally required for the GAFI free-zone or inland LLC registration and for the NVOCC license issued by the NWS/Transport Authority. A virtual office may be accepted only for very preliminary mail-forwarding prior to license issuance, but the permanent licensed office must be a physical location where the company maintains original books and records, corporate seal, and business files. For ISIC 5229 (NVOCC), the port authority or the Egyptian Ministry of Transport will conduct documentary substance review.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderately high. The risk of an unannounced physical on-site inspection within the first 12 months of operation is approximately 35% for freight-forwarding entities due to mandatory safety, customs, and container-security audits under Egyptian customs law and the Container Security Initiative (CSI) protocols.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 as amended by Law No. 4 of 2022 and Executive Regulations; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 for optional incentives; Commercial Code applicable registration provisions.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Foreign Trade (GAFI) – Companies Registration Directorate and One-Stop Shop.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association (system online notarization through GAFI's electronic registration portal).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an Egyptian LLC; the authorized capital stated in the Memorandum of Association must be fully subscribed, and cash subscriptions must be evidenced by a capital deposit certificate issued by a bank licensed by the Central Bank of Egypt or paid into GAFI's designated account prior to filing.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the sole incorporator approves the subscription of all issued shares of the company in accordance with the Memorandum of Association. The registered office is hereby established at the address stated in the Articles of Association and shall serve as the legal seat for service of process, statutory books, and tax correspondence. [Name] is appointed General Manager, [Name] is appointed Compliance Officer, and [Name] is appointed Chief Financial Officer, each with the powers specified in the Articles. The board is authorized to open corporate bank accounts, appoint an external auditor, obtain the NVOCC operating license, and execute all required government filings. This resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Corporate Form Screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop electronic portal and Egyptian Commercial Registry database.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three alternative proposed names through the GAFI online gateway; select the legal form Limited Liability Company (LLC); confirm the name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company; receive name reservation certificate; prepare the draft Memorandum and Articles of Association in Arabic and arrange notarization of the founders' signatures before a GAFI-certified notary.
required_dossiers: Copy of founders' passports or national ID cards
Proposed company name reservation request
Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association in Arabic
Power of attorney if a local nominee or legal representative signs
Certificate of appointment of authorized signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected because of similarity or violation of naming rules, re-submit up to three revised alternatives within 5 working days or file an objection with GAFI's Naming Committee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Subscription Evidence and Bank Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A commercial bank licensed by the Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) or GAFI's treasury account.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary capital subscription bank account in the company name; deposit the fully subscribed paid-up capital or obtain a bank certificate confirming the funds for future capital; obtain an official bank certificate of capital deposit. If in-kind capital is used, secure a certified valuation report and file it with GAFI.
required_dossiers: Memorandum of Association draft
Founders' passport copies
Bank account application forms
Source of funds statement for enhanced screening
Valid telecommunication and address proof for each appointor or manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests clarification on source of funds, provide additional KYC documents such as audited financial statements or bank reference letters, and refile the capital certificate with GAFI.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: E-Filing of Incorporation and Issuance of Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Deliver the complete incorporation application through GAFI's one-stop-shop, attaching the notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association, bank capital certificate, registered office lease or ownership proof, signed manager consents, and proof of payment of statutory fees. After statutory review, obtain the GAFI incorporation certificate, provisional tax card, and Commercial Registry preliminary extract.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Bank capital deposit certificate
Proof of registered office title or lease contract
Consent letters of appointed managers
Valid appointment resolutions and signatory specimen cards
Payment receipt for incorporation fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues a deficiency memorandum, cure the flagged defects within 15 working days by filing corrected documents or statutory declarations; appeal any refusal to the GAFI administrative review committee within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Register and Unified Tax Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Commercial Registry (within GAFI) and the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the commercial registration entry in the Egyptian Commercial Register; apply simultaneously with ETA for a unified tax identification number (TIN), tax card, and proof of stamp tax and stock transfer tax registration if applicable. The company's trade name, registered office, and managers must be accurately recorded.
required_dossiers: GAFI incorporation certificate
Commercial registry application form
Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Manager consent letters
Lease or ownership contract of registered office
Tax card application and corporate forms
Authorized signatory ID and passport copies
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify any data mismatches by submitting a formal correction memorandum to the Commercial Registry and ETA data correction unit; late registration penalties may be abated if corrected voluntarily within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Ministry of Transport – Maritime Transport Sector and the Egyptian Ports Authority as applicable.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the specialized NVOCC operating license application to the Maritime Transport Sector after incorporation. Attach the commercial registry extract, tax card, board resolution authorizing the license, proof of financial solvency or bank guarantee, insurance certificates, evidence of nominated sub-agents or overseas counterparties, and an operational plan covering container space procurement and bill-of-lading issuance procedures.
required_dossiers: Commercial register extract
GAFI incorporation certificate and tax card
Board resolution approving the NVOCC license application
Bank guarantee or audited net worth statement
Cargo liability insurance certificate
Pro-forma contracts with ocean carriers and destination agents
Containment plan for hazardous cargo handling if any
Nomination letters of responsible officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried by the Maritime Transport Sector Technical Committee, submit additional documentary clarifications within 20 working days; if the license is denied, request reconsideration or appeal to the Minister of Transport within 30 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Egyptian Ministry of Transport – Maritime Transport Sector (MTS) Freight Licensing Directorates.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Non-Vessel Operating Common Carrier (NVOCC) Freight Forwarding License

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B – Environmental Registration required for office-based NVOCC operations and light container consolidation facilities; a full Environmental Impact Assessment Report is mandated if warehousing or cargo-handling activity creates wastewater discharge, heavy vehicle traffic, noise, or contaminants exceeding ministerial thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Law No. 4 of 1994 for the Protection of the Environment, as amended, and Executive Regulations: industrial and sanitary wastewater must meet pollutant concentration limits (including TSS not exceeding 60 mg/L, BOD5 not exceeding 60 mg/L, and total petroleum hydrocarbons not exceeding 15 mg/L in non-sensitive water bodies); engine emissions from handling equipment and trucks must satisfy air quality standards for SO2, NOx, PM10, and visible smoke; any storage or transfer of dangerous goods requires an EEAA temporary waste handling permit and spill containment protocol.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The applicant must obtain a fire safety and civil defense clearance from the Egyptian Fire and Rescue Authority (Civil Defense) after inspection of the registered office, warehouses, and container consolidation yards; structural load inspection certificate from the local civil authority for any mezzanine or racking system; occupational health and workplace clearance from the Ministry of Manpower, including first aid facilities, fire extinguishers, emergency exit signage, sanitation standards, and workers' compensation registration.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) - Maslahat al-Dara'ib al-Misriyah; official digital portal https://www.eta.gov.eg; VAT e-invoicing and e-receipts clearance portal https://einvoicing.eta.gov.eg; governed by Tax Procedures Law No. 206 of 2020 and e-invoicing framework decrees.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Under Tax Procedures Law 206/2020, the LLC must self-register via the ETA unified e-services portal within 60 days of commercial commencement. Required submissions include notarized LLC bylaws, Commercial Registration extract, social insurance number, legal representative POA, and registered office evidence. The ETA issues a single Unified Tax Registration Number (UTRN) and tax card covering corporate income tax, VAT, payroll, and stamp duty. The LLC must also complete separate VAT registration once the statutory threshold is met and obtain an e-invoicing digital certificate before issuing taxable invoices.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (Egyptian LLC is a juridical taxpayer under Income Tax Law 91/2005; profits taxed at 22.5% corporate rate; no attribution to owners until distribution).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election exists. Statutory elections include: (1) group taxation consolidation for connected Egyptian companies under Income Tax Law 91/2005; (2) ETA-approved cash or accrual accounting basis elections for long-cycle service contracts; (3) investment incentive registration under Investment Law 72/2017 for eligible zones/activities; dividend distribution policy does not alter entity-level taxation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT - Value Added Tax under Law No. 67 of 2016 as amended
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 annual taxable turnover of goods and services (VAT Law 67/2016 as amended; registration mandatory upon crossing the threshold).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time clearance of e-invoices and e-receipts on ETA's digital stamping platform. The taxpayer integrates via ETA REST APIs, transmitting JSON documents with digital signature and QR code; each invoice receives an ETA clearance UUID before issuance to the client. Scanned documents without validated QR are non-compliant; customs exports are cross-referenced to cleared e-invoices in the customs single window.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT applies to goods physically exported from Egypt evidenced by customs export declarations and to exported services supplied to non-resident principals, including NVOCC ocean freight forwarding and box brokerage directly tied to export carriage and settled in foreign currency. Internationally rendered freight services qualify under the international transport zero-rating provisions; purely domestic logistics, warehousing, and Egyptian-port despatch services remain standard-rated at 14%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bayan Shaka) duly cleared in the Egyptian customs single window
Bill of Lading (Master or House) evidencing the export ocean leg
Inward Remittance Certificate from an Egyptian bank evidencing foreign currency repatriation
Commercial invoice and packing list signed by the declaring exporter
Freight forwarding service contract or booking note with the non-resident principal
ETA cleared e-invoice bearing the validated UUID for the zero-rated supply
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ETA performs post-export desk audits reconciling customs manifest data against e-invoices, bills of lading, and bank inward remittance certificates. If zero-rating is unjustified, the ETA recomputes 14% VAT on the full invoice value and imposes a 2% monthly late-payment surcharge plus administrative fines. Fraudulent documentation triggers tax evasion penalties under VAT Law 67/2016, including imprisonment and fines ranging from EGP 5,000 to EGP 50,000, multiples of tax evaded, suspension of e-invoicing API access, and customs licensing blacklisting.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) - the sole monetary, supervisory, and foreign-exchange authority under Law No. 194 of 2020 (Central Bank and Banking System Law) and its Executive Regulations (CBE Board Decision No. 2192 of 2021, as amended).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Since the March 2024 exchange-rate liberalization, the CBE operates a unified, market-determined float for the EGP against hard currencies; current-account transactions (trade settlement, freight invoices, agency fees) are freely executable through authorized banks at interbank or bank-offered rates without prior CBE licensing. Capital-account flows are convertible in principle under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017, but remain documentary-heavy: inbound equity subscriptions require a GAFI (General Authority for Investment and Free Zones) filing, an attested LLC contract, and a bank capital-attestation deposit; profit and dividend remittance requires audited financial statements, a valid tax card, tax filing and payment clearance, and source-of-funds documentation. In practice, bank-level compliance review and interbank FX availability create 1-5 business-day settlement friction, and effective USD liquidity tightens during CBE reserve-stabilization periods. For the NVOCC service model, ocean freight and brokerage fees qualify as invisible earnings and current-account services, repatriable once the receiving Egyptian bank holds the complete shipping file.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Egypt's current flex regime imposes no fixed mandatory surrender percentage: exporters may retain 100% of proceeds in USD or EUR in onshore FX accounts or convert at market rate without selling a statutory quota to the CBE. Repatriation timelines remain mandatory: proceeds from goods exports must be credited to a licensed Egyptian bank within 9 months from the bill-of-lading or export-customs date (Import/Export Law No. 118 of 1975, Article 46 and implementing CBE instructions); proceeds from service exports, including NVOCC freight, brokerage, and ancillary charges, must be collected within the contractual payment term, normally not exceeding 9 months from invoice date unless a CBE waiver is obtained. Each receipt must pass through the bank's foreign-exchange statistical system with the underlying contract, invoice, and cargo documents attached; non-repatriation, offshore parking of proceeds, or delayed conversion can trigger CBE sanctions, account restriction, and tax audit exposure.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account + Operational EGP/USD Accounts
Capital Escrow Account + Operational EGP/USD Accounts
Capital Escrow Account + Operational EGP/USD Accounts

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: LOW as a primary clearing rail; CONDITIONAL as an ancillary offshore collection pipe. Non-CBE-licensed digital EMIs (Wise, Airwallex, Payoneer, Revolut) cannot hold EGP or clear through Egypt's SWIFT/RTGS ecosystem; Egyptian receiving banks will flag, delay, or reject credits routed from an unlicensed EMI unless the full underlying freight document set is pre-submitted. The practical approach is to use an EMI authorized by a reputable regulator (FCA, CySEC, or equivalent) only for collecting small overseas brokerage commissions from low-risk jurisdictions, then sweep funds weekly to the onshore NVOCC USD account with the carriage documentation embedded in the wire reference.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Hybrid but practically mandatory in-country visit. Under Anti-Money Laundering and Combating the Financing of Terrorism Law No. 80 of 2002 (as amended) and CBE KYC instructions, every Egyptian corporate account requires the bank to identify the ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) and authorized signatories. A locally resident general manager or Egypt-resident signatory must attend the branch interview in person. Non-resident shareholders or directors may be verified via remote video call together with notarized and legalized powers of attorney (Apostille or consular certification acceptable), but most Tier 1 banks still require original passports and corporate documents to be physically examined by a compliance officer before the account is activated. Pure remote account opening for a 100% foreign-owned LLC is not practicable; a single Cairo visit covering the GAFI file, bank KYC interview, and capital attestation within 3-5 business days is the recommended execution path.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-Based Money Laundering alert triggered by freight invoicing diverging from cargo value, or by the NVOCC margin appearing anomalous.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original shipment file comprising the shipper/consignee commercial invoice, packing list, export customs declaration, non-negotiable bill of lading, master carrier bill of lading, freight quotation from the ocean carrier, bank settlement statement matching the exact freight amount, and a board-approved commercial tariff demonstrating the 3-5% NVOCC margin.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party payment arrangement where an importer's bank, buyer, or overseas agent settles the freight invoice instead of the contractual shipper.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed tripartite payment-mandate letter from the contractual counterparty and the actual payor; underlying sale or transport contract; retained email archive evidencing the payment instruction; and a ledger reconciliation demonstrating no circular or unexplained fund flow.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Exposure to UN/OFAC/EU-sanctioned or high-risk jurisdictions, including Sudan, Libya, Syria, Yemen, or transshipment cargoes passing conflict zones.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Live sanctions-screening report from an automated World-Check or Dow Jones/O FAC list verification for every counterparty and vessel; bill of lading and customs entry showing genuine origin and destination; cargo-beneficiary attestation; Egyptian Ministry of Transport / General Authority for Maritime Transport NVOCC license; and a written policy prohibiting cash payments and uncleared parties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent EGP-USD round-tripping or rapid same-day FX conversion flagged as possible unlicensed money-changing or money laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved treasury policy memorandum; FX conversion scheduled against documented USD freight payment obligations, including carrier invoices, port tariffs, and bunker surcharges; interbank FX order ticket from the same authorized bank; and a 12-month cash-flow forecast of the freight-forwarding operation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Foreign shareholders fund the Egyptian LLC by a SWIFT MT103 from the investor's own bank account to the capital-attestation (escrow) account opened at the selected CBE-licensed bank. The remittance must carry a purpose of payment such as 'Inward Direct Investment - Equity Capital' together with the applicable CBE statistical purpose code for FDI equity, the LLC name, and the GAFI investment file number. The bank's compliance file must hold the LLC contract (Articles of Association), GAFI registration notification, copy of the capital-deposit certificate issued by the notary or bank, board or shareholder resolution on officer authorization, passport copies of UBOs, and the company's written request for capital attestation. Upon matching the remittance to the attested amount, the bank issues the capital certificate and transfers the funds to the operational account, registering the transaction with CBE statistics. The treasury verification step is to obtain the bank's irrevocable inward-remittance confirmation before GAFI stamps the share certificates.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outgoing settlements of NVOCC obligations, including ocean carrier freight, container deposits, port charges, overseas agency commissions, and slot purchases, are executed predominantly by SWIFT MT103 direct transfer because Egypt's free-float regime removes prior CBE approval for service transactions. The bank requires the carrier's commercial invoice and debit note, the underlying booking or service contract, and confirmation of sufficient EGP/USD liquidity; recurring payments to core carriers may be covered by a standing-order facility after one full KYC and trade-file review. For high-value charter or slot-purchase commitments, an irrevocable commercial Letter of Credit (MT700) can be issued against CBE-reportable documentation; for smaller contracted maritime agents, SWIFT MT103 with trade-purpose coding remains the most efficient rail. On the Egyptian side, the CBE's real-time gross settlement system for EGP and the SWIFT network for USD/EUR are the formal clearing layers; the Arab Regional Payment System (Buna) is a secondary regional alternative for EGP, AED, and SAR corridors.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore outright delivery forwards (USD/EGP and EUR/EGP) with documented underlying freight and trade cash flows, tenors typically up to 12 months, executed at a CBE-licensed bank under Law No. 194 of 2020.
FX swaps (USD/EGP) for short-dated treasury rebalancing and for covering mismatched freight collection and payment cycles, available as spot/forward or tom-next structures up to 6 months.

Cross-currency swaps for long-dated USD/EGP commercial liabilities, available on a case-by-case exemption and approval basis; offshore NDFs in EGP are not permitted onshore and should be avoided to prevent bank compliance flags.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual audited financial statements and board report filed with GAFI
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the Annual General Meeting; AGM must occur no later than 6 months after fiscal year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties escalate from EGP 2,000 per day up to a maximum of EGP 50,000; persistent failure can trigger administrative filings and director liability

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Form No. 11 for legal entities)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after the fiscal year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of EGP 1,000 to EGP 2,000 per month; interest at 1.5% per month on defaulted tax; criminal penalties for deliberate failure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial ownership confirmation and UBO register update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March following each calendar year; additionally within 15 days of any share transfer or UBO change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines ranging from EGP 20,000 to EGP 100,000 for failure to file; suspension of corporate registrations may follow

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual NVOCC / freight forwarding operating licence renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Maritime Transport Sector, Ministry of Transport, Egypt
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Renewal application must be submitted at least 60 days before the licence expiry (typically 31 December of each year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-renewal results in immediate suspension of freight forwarding privileges; possible revocation of NVOCC licence and administrative fines up to EGP 100,000

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: All Egyptian LLCs are statutorily required to appoint a registered auditor and file audited financial statements; no size-based exemption exists under the Companies Law.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), substantially aligned with IFRS

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: UBO data must be confirmed annually through GAFI's electronic register. Any share transfer or change of beneficial ownership must be updated within 15 days. Failure to comply is subject to fines of EGP 20,000–100,000.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holiday for standard LLCs. Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 permits a deduction of up to 50% of taxable income for new projects in certain governorates/sectors. Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCEZ) projects may enjoy customs and VAT benefits, but corporate income tax relief remains subject to Investment Law provisions and does not universally exempt LLC income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Tax Return Form No. 21 (Corporate Income Tax Return for commercial and industrial activities) submitted through the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) e-portal at www.eta.gov.eg
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within four months after the end of the fiscal year (Law 91 of 2005, Article 31). Extension available upon prior approval for consolidated or foreign-source accounting files.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue derived from Egyptian sources (freight forwarding and NVOCC service fees).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholder does not file this return. The Egyptian LLC reports all Egyptian-source revenue in this box; invoices and contracts must be retained to evidence source.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from foreign-source activities attributable to the permanent establishment of the Egyptian LLC.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders include treaty-derived income according to the LLC's accounts. Foreign tax credits may be claimed for taxes paid abroad on this segment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct operating costs and deductible business expenses (ocean freight, port charges, container handling, subcontractor fees).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expense deductions require supporting documentation. Payments to related non-resident parties must be priced on an arm's-length basis and flagged if exceeding the transfer pricing documentation threshold.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Dividends, interest, royalties, and other portfolio investment income received by the LLC.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders should separately monitor outbound distributions under the dividend WHT regime. Inbound income may be exempt or treaty-reduced if properly disclosed through Schedule for withholding tax credits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing incurs a penalty equal to 2% of the aggregate tax due per month of delay (capped at 50% of the tax due), plus a fixed minimum penalty of EGP 2,000. False or incomplete returns may trigger additional penalties of up to EGP 20,000 and criminal fines under Law 91 of 2005.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on dividends and profit distributions paid by Egyptian resident companies to non-resident shareholders (Law 91 of 2005).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced dividend WHT rate under an applicable double tax treaty (DTA), the non-resident shareholder must (1) obtain a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the home jurisdiction, (2) submit the TRC and a completed WHT relief application to the paying Egyptian entity before dividend distribution, and (3) file a declaration with the Egyptian Tax Authority confirming beneficial ownership. The ETA may grant a reduced rate certificate or require a refund after payment if the statutory rate was applied.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory domestic rates: 20% for interest and 20% for royalties paid to non-residents. Treaty rates commonly range from 0% to 15% for interest and 10% to 15% for royalties, depending on the applicable DTA. For freight forwarding and NVOCC activities, payments for container software licenses, slot charter royalties, and intercompany loan interest face these rates unless treaty relief is obtained.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File required when the aggregate value of controlled transactions in a tax year exceeds EGP 30 million. Master File required when the multinational group's consolidated revenue exceeds EGP 1 billion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not operate a formal Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime akin to the UAE, but the Egyptian Tax Authority applies general anti-abuse rules and substance-over-form principles under Law 91 of 2005. An Egyptian NVOCC LLC must maintain physical staff, operating bank accounts, board management, and decision-making records for local operations; a shell with no genuine freight forwarding activity faces reclassification and penalty exposure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately underreporting maritime freight revenue, concealing commissions from carrier principals, or overstating deductible subcontractor payments to avoid corporate income tax liability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imposition of the avoided tax amount plus a 100% penalty on the evaded tax (Law 91 of 2005, Article 133). Criminal fines of up to EGP 50,000 and/or imprisonment for the responsible officers may also apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate taxes if they approved false accounts. Egyptian courts permit piercing the corporate veil where fraud is proven; officers face personal civil restitution, travel bans by blacklisting with tax authority, and imprisonment of up to three years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Egyptian LLC operates without any physical office, qualified maritime staff, real operational decision-making, or active bank account transactions solely to route profits from ocean freight to a low-tax jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disallowance of claimed expenses, recharacterization of profits under general anti-avoidance rules, and a penalty of up to 30% of the adjusted tax amount. The Tax Authority may also deem the LLC to be a permanent establishment of its parent if substance is lacking.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face restoration orders to make good any unpaid taxes arising from artificial profit allocation; travel bans may be issued by the ETA for non-payment, and criminal charges for facilitation of tax evasion can extend to imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging international freight forwarding affiliate fees, container slot lease payments, or intercompany management charges at non-arm's-length rates that shift profit outside Egypt and cause ETA to adjust taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA may upwardly adjust the taxable income and apply a 30% adjustment penalty on the additional tax due. Underestimated TP documentation penalties range from EGP 10,000 to EGP 50,000 for failure to submit a Local File.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or approve TP documentation containing false figures may be personally obliged for the adjusted tax and penalties; criminal sanctions arise if willful intent to evade tax is demonstrated, including travel bans and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing profits or paying interest, royalties, or fees to non-resident shareholders without deducting and remitting the applicable statutory or treaty-related WHT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Withholding agent (Egyptian LLC) is liable for the full WHT amount plus monthly delay surcharge of 2% per month (capped at 50% of tax). Violations may trigger a service-provider payment ban and administrative blocking of corporate filings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and senior managers can be held personally liable for unremitted WHT where they controlled the distribution process. Egyptian law permits travel restrictions and asset attachment for delinquent officers; in severe cases, imprisonment for misappropriation of withheld taxes.
